previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral below-knee amputations, and a history of recurrent infections was admitted for abnormal lab results showing elevated liver enzymes, hyperkalemia, and acute kidney injury. She felt well without abdominal pain or systemic symptoms. The transaminitis was attributed to recent antibiotic and statin use, all of which were discontinued. Hyperkalemia resolved with kayexalate and IV fluids, and kidney function stabilized. Liver enzymes improved during the stay, and no imaging was needed. She remained on oral vancomycin for ongoing C. difficile treatment and continued her baseline medications. A urine culture showed yeast and probable Enterococcus, but without symptoms, no new treatment was started. The PICC line was noted to have migrated slightly but remained functional. She was discharged home with nursing services after a two-day stay, with instructions to follow up on liver tests and colorectal evaluation for persistent stool in the vaginal vault.

for treatment of presumed bacteremia. Her PICC line had been 
removed earlier in the day. The infectious disease service was 
consulted and recommended for a 5 to 7 day course of intravenous 
antibiotics. Ultimately, the bacteria was speciated as coagulase

contaminant or true bacteremia. She completed a course of

discharge.

use, here to assess for hepatic abnormality.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen most recently of ___, and abdominal ultrasound of
___.

ABDOMINAL ULTRASOUND:  The liver again demonstrates normal echotexture and
architecture, with no focal liver lesion seen.  The main portal vein is patent
with normal hepatopetal flow.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary
ductal dilatation, with the common duct measuring 4 mm.  The gallbladder is
contracted and contain echogenic stones.  The visualized portions of the
pancreatic head and body show no focal abnormality; the pancreatic tail is
obscured by overlying bowel gas.  The visualized aorta is of normal caliber. 
Views of the intrahepatic IVC show no abnormality.  No ascites is seen in the
upper abdomen.

1.  Normal sonogram of the liver.
